question.text: Enterprise Value (EV) is best described as:

answer.text: The market capitalisation of a listed company only
The book value per share multiplied by outstanding shares
The value of just the preference shares of a company
The debt-free, cash-free value of the operating business — the value of total capital regardless of whether debt or equity finances it

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.4.1: 'Enterprise value (EV) is the debt-free/cash free value of the operating business. ... EV is the value of the total capital in the company or business regardless of whether it is debt or equity capital.' It captures the whole operating value before financing decisions. The Trap: Market cap = equity value (not EV); book value x shares = book value of equity; preference shares alone is one component. EV = Equity Value + Net Debt + Preference Capital. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical. XV (RA) tests with more M&A context. EV/EBITDA is the most cited M&A multiple globally. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching an acquisition to your IC, always quote EV (not equity value) because EV is financing-structure neutral. Debt assumption is then a separate negotiation line in the SPA.
